source.title: The Lazy Neuron Phenomenon: On Emergence of Activation Sparsity in Transformers
source.authors: Zong-xiao Li; Chong You; Srinadh Bhojanapalli; Daliang Li; A. S. Rawat; Sashank J. Reddi; Kenneth Q Ye; Felix Chern; Felix X. Yu; Ruiqi Guo; Surinder Kumar

record.tranche_reason: Appendix E reports training accuracy for two-layer MLPs trained on finite random inputs and random labels, bearing on fitting random labels. It does not reproduce the standard Transformer/image experiments in the original sources.
record.gate_note: The paper’s main random-label experiment reports activation sparsity, not fitting accuracy, so it is not a row for these claim versions. Appendix E reports training accuracy on random data; include those results. Other activation-sparsity measurements do not test the listed claim versions.
record.test_reason: Appendix E directly measures random-label training accuracy in a new setting: two-layer ReLU MLPs on fixed uniform-random images. Figure 8 also bears on learning signal before memorizing noise, and Table 1 measures test-performance degradation with increasing label corruption.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes Appendix E: sufficiently wide two-layer MLPs perfectly fit fixed random data, and sparsity varies with fitting and width. The paper's broader conclusion concerns prevalent activation sparsity, its possible origin in training dynamics, and benefits from enforcing sparsity. Its noisy-label experiments additionally show late overfitting by vanilla ViT and improved generalization with Top-k sparsity.
record.recipe_differences: Uses two-layer MLP experiments with random inputs and random labels in Appendix E; does not reproduce the original deep-network image-labeling setup.
record.method_sensitivity: Training accuracy and activation sparsity vary with model width and training dataset; larger learning rates produce sparser activations.

fits_no_version.finding: Top-128 ViT improves final test accuracy under label noise relative to vanilla ViT.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Enforcing activation sparsity can improve generalization under corrupted training labels.

record.code_released: https://github.com/google-research/t5x and Scenic codebase are named; a study-specific results URL is not stated.
record.problems: The random-data fitting evidence is for two-layer MLPs rather than the standard deep networks in the claim. The cited accuracy results are presented in figures without exact values in the text, and test error is not reported for these random-data experiments.
record.rows_left_out: Activation-sparsity measurements for random labels, random images, and infinite data (Figure 5) do not report the fitting behavior required by the versions. Other sparsity-only results throughout the paper likewise do not measure a listed claim version.

untested.parts: Chance-level test error and fitting fully randomized labels on natural inputs are not established by Appendix E. Hyperparameters are shared across its dataset conditions, but architecture width is varied.
Relative time to fit true versus random labels and convergence slowdown across corruption fractions.
Zero-error fitting of shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian inputs. Appendix E instead uses uniform-random pixels.
Perfect training fit throughout a corruption sweep, behavior at complete corruption, and a sufficiently detailed sweep to establish smooth degradation toward chance.
Whether weight decay, dropout, and augmentation prevent random-label fitting, and whether removing them harms clean-label generalization.
Separate learning trajectories for correctly labeled and corrupted examples; direct identification of which examples are memorized.

missing.what: Vanilla ViT test accuracy at 0%, 40%, and 80% random-label corruption: 74.85%, 59.44%, and 25.35%. These measure the degradation component of V4.

At 80% label corruption, vanilla ViT begins overfitting around 45,000 steps: training accuracy continues rising while evaluation accuracy falls. Record the trajectory as indirect evidence about signal learning before memorization, without claiming separate clean/noisy-example measurements.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source. Sparsity-only experiments do not establish random-label fitting. Figure 8 provides indirect evidence for V6 through generalization and overfitting trajectories, rather than direct clean-versus-noisy learning curves.

versions.untested_parts: Tests random-label fitting only in two-layer MLPs on random inputs. Does not test standard deep networks on randomly relabeled natural images, test error at chance, or whether fitting requires changes from the true-label setup.
Training-time comparisons and convergence slowdown with increasing label corruption are not reported.
Does not report fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs to zero training error.
Does not report training and test error across a sweep from clean to fully corrupted labels.
Does not test whether weight decay, dropout, or data augmentation prevent random-label fitting or whether removing them harms true-label generalization.
Does not compare learning of real-data patterns with subsequent memorization of noisy or random labels over training.
